name: Ohio

notes: Food for consumption off the premises is exempt, candy included, but soft drinks and dietary supplements are taxed at the full rate, which is not counted here.

Restaurants: only food eaten on the premises is taxed; carryout and drive-through food is exempt (soft drinks are taxed either way), which is not taken out here, so the restaurant figures, quick-service most, overstate the tax.
Alcohol: beer, wine and spirits are taxed at the general rate, spirits from state agency stores included.
Cigarettes and other tobacco are taxed at the general rate, on top of their excise taxes.
Household supplies: children's diapers, baby wipes, cribs, car seats and strollers are exempt (since October 1, 2023), which is not taken out here.
Personal care products: menstrual products are exempt (since April 1, 2020), which is not taken out here.

Barber and beauty services: haircuts and hair coloring and styling are not taxed, but manicures, pedicures, skin care, hair removal, tanning, massage, tattooing and piercing are, which is not counted here.
Clothing is taxed. The 2026 back-to-school holiday ran August 7 to 9 (clothing up to $75); a 15-day holiday on most items up to $500 is set for August 1 to 15, 2027 (reported).
Laundry and dry cleaning are taxed, except at self-service laundries, which is not taken out here.

Gasoline is exempt from sales tax; the per-gallon motor fuel tax, left out here as an excise tax, is suspended (cut to a ten-thousandth of a cent a gallon) from October 4, 2026 to January 2, 2027 (House Bill 519; ODT).
Auto repair labor: taxed (FTA 2017 survey answer).

Resort areas may tax businesses' gross receipts at 0.5% to 1.5% (up to 2.5% with a vote), as Put-in-Bay does, and Cuyahoga County taxes alcohol by the gallon and cigarettes by the cigarette; neither is counted here (ORC 5739.101; the places' pages say more).

Hotel stays pay the sales tax plus city and county lodging taxes (Columbus 5.1% plus the Franklin County convention facilities authority's 4.9%; Cleveland 3% plus Cuyahoga County 5.5% in the state's 2018 table, the latest published), which are not counted here.
gaps: Ohio has no city sales taxes; the local rate is the county rate plus any transit authority.
The rate file lists the current rate of Holmes County only through a date before April 1, 2027, with nothing after it (a renewal may not be filed yet); the current rate is used.

39035: Cuyahoga County also taxes alcohol by the gallon and cigarettes by the cigarette for its sports venues, and cigarettes again for arts and culture (raised from 30 to 70 cents a pack by voters in November 2024, Issue 55; Ideastream); these per-unit taxes aren't counted. The county and Cleveland are drawing up a plan to fund repairs at Rocket Arena and Progressive Field that could include a higher sales tax and higher alcohol and cigarette taxes; nothing has been decided (Ideastream, October 19, 2026).
39075: Holmes County's 1.25% county rate is listed in the state's rate file only through March 31, 2027, with nothing after it; it is counted here, as in effect now.
39165: Warren County's rate rose to 7.25% on October 1, 2026 (Ohio Department of Taxation), and is counted here; the state's rate file lists the increase only through September 30, 2027.
3965032: Put-in-Bay village has taxed businesses' gross receipts as a resort area since 1995, at 1.5% since 2001 (Supreme Court of Ohio, 2022); Put-in-Bay Township levies one too. On May 5, 2026 voters in both approved raising the tax from 1.5% to 2%, as the Ottawa County Board of Elections' list of issues describes it. It isn't counted: it is a tax on businesses' receipts rather than a sales tax, and when the 2% starts wasn't found.

programs: Ohio has no statewide map of Enterprise Zones or Community Reinvestment Areas; they are mapped for Columbus (its enterprise zones and commercial reinvestment areas), Stark County and Lucas County. Columbus's housing reinvestment areas, which cover 244 census tracts across the city in three tiers, aren't drawn.

Special improvement districts are mapped for Columbus (six). Its two downtown districts, Capital Crossroads and Discovery, closed November 1, 2025, as reported, and are not on the city's map. No map was found for Cleveland's districts (among them Downtown, Gordon Square, Ohio City, Kamm's Corners, Superior Arts and University Circle) or Cincinnati's (Downtown and Over-the-Rhine).
Tax increment financing districts are mapped for Cincinnati, Franklin County and two of Cleveland's (East Side and Shore to Core to Shore); Cleveland's other TIF districts aren't mapped.

warn.text: Sandusky draws many visitors (Cedar Point and the Lake Erie shore), but the area shown here isn't flagged as a visitor economy: its seasonal homes and its lodging places per resident fall under the flag's cutoffs, though one of its 8 census tracts is flagged on its own. Visitors' spending is part of Sandusky's local sales, so its retention rates likely overstate how much of residents' own spending stays local.
